scenes.headline: How a Kalman filter fuses a guess and a sensor
scenes.sub: The predict-update cycle, the gain, and the step up to LiDAR-inertial SLAM.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pipit! Here's how a Kalman filter fuses a noisy sensor and a drifting model into one estimate that knows how unsure it is.

scenes.label: The key fact
scenes.text: Combining two Gaussian estimates yields a third Gaussian that is sharper than either input.
scenes.say: The key fact: multiply two Gaussian guesses, the prediction and the measurement, and you get a third that's sharper than either.

scenes.title: Fusing two numbers
scenes.text: μ = μ1 + K(μ2 − μ1),  K = σ1² / (σ1² + σ2²)
scenes.say: Here's the update, for a single number.

parts.say: Take how far the measurement disagrees.

parts.note: the gain: which source is more certain
parts.say: And move a fraction K of the way. Trust the sensor, and K goes to one. Trust the prediction, and it goes to zero.

steps.say: The filter holds a belief: a state, like position and velocity, and a covariance saying how unsure it is.
Predict pushes the belief through the motion model. The estimate moves, and the uncertainty grows by the process noise, Q.
Then a measurement arrives, with its own noise, R. The gain weighs the two, and the uncertainty shrinks.
The corrected belief is the starting point for the next step. Predict, update, forever.

items.say: For nonlinear systems, linearize at the current estimate with Jacobians, and run the same equations.
If one linearization isn't enough, relinearize after the update and repeat until it converges.
For rotations, track the error in the tangent space. Together, that's the engine inside FAST-LIO2.

scenes.text: Predict inflates the belief; update multiplies it by the measurement and sharpens it. That loop runs real robots.

recap: Two Gaussians fuse into a sharper one
Predict grows uncertainty, update shrinks it
scenes.say: To recap: fuse two Gaussians, alternate predict and update, and linearize when the world bends.
